newsitem.title: USA: NYC $558 mln GOs, $300 mln Euronotes A-minus - Fitch.
newsitem.headline: NYC $558 mln GOs, $300 mln Euronotes A-minus - Fitch.

text.p: New York City's general obligation bonds, fiscal 1997 series H $550,000,000 tax-exempt bonds and $8,000,000 taxable bonds and $300,000,000 floating rate Euronotes due 1998 through 2002 are rated 'A-' by Fitch Investors Service.
The notes are general obligations of the city and will be offered through negotiation on or about Jan. 14 through a syndicate led by Goldman Sachs International.
The domestic issue will be offered on Jan. 14 through a syndicate led by Goldman, Sachs & Co. Proceeds from the combined new issues will refund outstanding city general obligation bonds.

Additionally, the approximately $26 billion in outstanding general obligation bonds are affirmed at 'A-'. The city's economic and revenue improvements have exceeded expectations, resulting in higher revenue estimates for the current fiscal year and allowing the removal of what were risky assumptions in the current year's budget.

Additionally, in the November modification of the budget the city implemented ongoing spending cuts and reduced outyear projected budget gaps. Nevertheless, the revenue increase this year is largely tied to the securities industry and cannot be counted on for subsequent years' budgets.

Consequently, the magnitude of the projected outyear funding gaps still remains large -- rising to $3 billion, or 9% of projected revenues, by 2000 -- constituting a vulnerability, particularly given the volatility of the securities industry. These outyear uncertainties are reflected in a negative outlook.
The floating rate Euronotes bear interest at a rate tied to London Interbank Offered Rate for three month United States dollar deposits payable quarterly.

While the interest rate cap is high at 35%, the magnitude of the issue relative to the city's debt structure and budget resources is minimal. Furthermore, the duration of the notes will be short, maturing in five years with an average life of three and half years after scheduled redemptions.
